summary: 1. The Excavator-398 approach incident (Sep 21, Richard/Production Supervisor) moves from an open leadership-response item to a scheduled, structured investigation. 2. Two new sources — a PM pre-investigation meeting and Peter's own detailed investigation brief — confirm the classification (Line of Fire, Maaden Life Saving Rules), set the interview for Sep 23 14:30, 45 minutes max, run by Safety Superintendent Collins and HR with Peter explicitly excluded from the room. 3. The site's approach procedure surfaces in full for the first time in this KB: 50 m (radio the operator), 30 m (confirm bucket down), 10 m (confirm operator out of cab). 4. A Fair Culture evidence framework shows every gate — deliberate harm, D&A testing, foresight, rule-workability, personal history — still open, and the existing operator statement is flagged as currently unusable (merged questionnaire answers, no witness or independent translator). 5. Richard has not been suspended as of this pass. 6. See [[people-machinery-interaction]] (primary record) and [[safety-inspection-patterns]]. 2. 7. A Stage 5 870RL hanging-edge clearance did not fully remove the hazard; the planned 830RL overspill loading was suspended and formally reported to the client. 8. This is the primary written source behind a Task Feedback Log entry from Sep 20 that had no Wiki article attached to it at the time — it now supplies the missing context, including that loading had not yet resumed as of the record's writing. 9. See [[overspill-material-management]]. 3. Drilling is running ahead of its own daily plan (~3,000 m/day vs. 2,600 m/day) with four days targeted to clear blocks 160 remnant and 161, against a stepped next-month volume target (1.85M → 1.95M → 2M). A material-sourcing risk surfaces: the current romper (beach) supply will not sustain the full week, with three alternatives under discussion and no decision made. See [[blasting-and-drilling]]. 4. A new site-level diagnostic tool — an hourly per-excavator productivity log with truck/operator gap root-cause tracking (dispatch allocation vs. truck availability vs. operator shortage) — targets the standing 85%/90% utilization-vs-availability gap this KB has tracked through September. Templates are currently blank. See [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 5. Task Feedback Log: 80/80 rows Processed, zero unprocessed, no mismatches. Nothing to mark this pass. 6. Important References: the D8 dozer loan request (registered at index level only by the morning's dashboard-scoped pass) is now fully synthesized — Maaden's stated premise that the ADW wheel dozer's repair is nearly done is wrong; the unit (WD-145) is at its 57th consecutive day down. Joe Coleman's reply does not correct the record. See [[fleet-availability-utilization]] and `Outputs/important-references-analysis_2026-09-23.md`. 7. A life-saving-rules refresher session names the site's full nine-rule list explicitly for the first time in this KB's tracking, triggered by a finding that personnel know the rules exist but can't clearly explain field application. A three-week pit-rescue steering-committee exercise is planned for January. See [[safety-inspection-patterns]]. 8. Two candidate meeting-note pages created 2026-09-23 were checked and found empty (no content at fetch time) — not ingested, flagged for a later re-check. A JD (Job Description Form) for the Production Superintendent role, signed by Peter Dotto, was found cloud-only in RAW/HR, hydrated, and OCR'd — a standard administrative role document with no new operational content, registered for provenance only. Four Notion Notes & References rows were ingested (the two above plus the productivity log and a personal IMS training reference); nine other rows in that database remain confirmed non-mining/personal.
